subject: Post-demo econ checkpoint — token footprint & startup pricing options
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@ledger.ai>, Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@ledger.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo econ checkpoint — token footprint & startup pricing options

Hi Samir / Aisha — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and next steps from my side.

Call recap (short):
- Primary use: contextual summarization and search reranker for customer chat logs.
- Estimated steady-state volume: 0.5M — 1.5M tokens/mo; peak experiments could push to ~3M/mo in Q4.
- Latency requirement: P95 < 450ms for routed inference.
- Success metric: 30% reduction in search latency + 10% reduction in support handle time.

Pricing conversation notes / asks:
- You asked for target $/1M tokens and how startup credits & committed-use discounts stack.
- To give a clean picture I attached a short pricing worksheet and our startup terms (see attachments).

Prelim options (illustrative):
- On-demand (no commitment): $4,200 per 1M tokens
- 12-month committed tier (volume-based bands): ~$2,800 per 1M (≈ 33% off on-demand) for agreed monthly baseline
- 24-month multi‑year commit: ~$2,200 per 1M (≈ 48% off on-demand) with milestone-based rebates
- Startup program: founder credit (one-time) + 90 days of usage credit — credits generally apply to on-demand consumption and are not stackable with certain multi-year rebate structures; we can clarify eligibility.

Questions for you so we can turn this into a clean quote:
1) Confirm likely committed baseline you could sign to today (e.g., 1M/mo vs 3M/mo).
2) Target $/1M that keeps you comfortable (range is fine).
3) Any procurement constraints or required PO timing (finance windows)?
4) Do you plan to pursue Dedicated capacity later (we can show migration cost delta).

Next steps: if you confirm 1–2 above I’ll loop in Marissa (sales lead) to put a formal quote and DocuSign. Ben is cc’d for unit-econ input.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi | Account Executive | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0178

Attachments: redwood-pricing-worksheet.xlsx, redwood-startup-terms.pdf
From: Samir Patel <samir@ledger.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@ledger.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo econ checkpoint — token footprint & startup pricing options

Irene — thanks for the clear notes. A few quick clarifications from our side:

1) Budget / target: our VC board asked us to target <$10k/month initially (runway-friendly) and stretch to $20k/mo if we lock material discounts. Translating to $/1M, that implies a target of ~$3k–$6k per 1M depending on actual monthly volume.
2) Baseline we could commit to today: 1M tokens/mo for the next 12 months with clear option to ramp to 3M/mo after product-market fit.
3) Question on stacking: is the startup founder credit stackable with a 12-month committed discount? If not, can you show the blended effective $/1M for the first 3 months (with startup credit) and for the following months under a committed rate?
4) Procurement: we can get a PO within 2 weeks once commercial terms are agreed; preferred to get pricing locked by end of next week.

Ask: can you produce a simple comparison table (on-demand vs 12mo commit vs 24mo commit) with effective $/1M at our 1M and 3M volumes, and show the first-90-day blended rate if startup credit applies? That will help our CFO.

Thanks —
Samir
Samir Patel | Head of Product | LedgerAI
samir@ledger.ai | (646) 555-0199

Attachment: ledgerai-internal-budget.xlsx (internal)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@ledger.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo econ checkpoint — token footprint & startup pricing options

Thanks Samir — looping in Marissa to put a formal quote together and Ben to sanity-check unit-econ. Quick answers inline and a small worked example below.

Stacking & startup program basics:
- Our startup founder credit (one-time) is separate from the standard committed-use discount; however, credits are generally applied to on-demand consumption first.
- For a 12-month committed agreement we can be flexible on how the initial credit is modeled (e.g., applied to month 1–3 on top of committed rate vs applied only to overage). We’ll show both options in the worksheet.

Illustrative worked example (you said 1M baseline):
- On-demand: $4,200 / 1M
- 12mo commit baseline (1M/mo): $2,800 / 1M
- If we apply a $6k founder credit over first 90 days to on-demand, blended first-90-day effective cost at 1M/mo becomes: ((4,200*3) - 6,000)/3 = $3,400 / 1M (on-demand + credit)
- If you choose to apply the founder credit to the committed rate instead we’ll show that blended math as well (but guardrails apply).

Action for Marissa: Marissa — can you produce the simple table Samir requested showing 1M and 3M volumes across the three pricing pillars plus first-90-day blended scenarios? Please include required legal/term highlights (startup eligibility, credit expiry, cancellation windows).

Irene

Subject: Re: Post-demo econ checkpoint — token footprint & startup pricing options

Samir — thanks, I put together the comparatives and attached the worksheet + startup terms. Key highlights (executive summary):

Executive summary:
- If LedgerAI signs a 12-month commitment at 1M/mo baseline we can offer $2,800 / 1M for the baseline band.
- For 3M/mo baseline the blended banding drops to $2,350 / 1M (volume bands applied).
- 24-month commit pricing reduces to $2,200 / 1M across the same bands (requires 12mo minimum notice on ramp semantics).
- Startup founder credit: $6,000 one-time credit applied to first 90 days of usage. It can be structured to apply to on-demand buckets or to offset committed first-month invoices depending on which preserves accounting treatment for LedgerAI.

Attached: redwood-pricing-worksheet.xlsx (summary table & 1-3-yr scenarios)
Attached: redwood-startup-terms.pdf (eligibility, expiration, non‑stacking clauses)

Simple comparison (effective $/1M) — illustrative
- 1M/mo
  - On-demand: $4,200
  - 12mo commit: $2,800 (effective after signing)
  - 12mo commit + first-90-day $6k credit applied to committed invoices: month1–3 blended = $1,800 / 1M equivalent for months 1–3, then $2,800 thereafter (example structure)
- 3M/mo
  - On-demand: $4,200
  - 12mo commit (banded): $2,350
  - 24mo commit (banded): $2,200

Compliance & SLA: Standard enterprise SLA is available for Dedicated and Dedicated-ready accounts; hosted SaaS agreements include 99.5% uptime and support SLAs — we’ll put exact language in the SOW.

Next steps for closure this week:
1) Samir: confirm whether you want the $6k credit applied to the committed invoices (recommended for cashflow benefit) or to on-demand buckets.
2) I’ll send a formal quote (HubSpot + DocuSign) once you confirm baseline (1M vs 3M) and credit treatment.
3) Procurement: if PO timing is tight we can do an order form with a placeholder start date to reserve pricing pending signature.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567
Quote (placeholder): https://app.redwood.ai/quotes/DL-2027-091

Marissa Cole | Sales Director | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0112

Marissa / Irene — thanks for the worked examples and the clarity. We’ll sign a 12-month commitment at 1M/mo baseline and want the $6k founder credit applied to the committed invoices (months 1–3). Two asks to close this week:

1) Please send DocuSign with that structure + the SOW language referencing the ability to add Dedicated later (we expect to evaluate in Q4).
2) Confirm SLA page reference and expected lead time for Dedicated migration (ballpark).

If you can send the DocuSign by EOD Thursday I’ll route to our finance team for PO issuance next week.

Appreciate the fast follow-up —
Samir
